why.net/grug/minecraft/core/GrugForcedNormal: The decision the runner makes before a marked test's first tick: appliesTo is asked for every test, but capabilitiesToTurnOff and matchesFound run only for a test whose loader is forced, which a dedicated server never is. The one coverage test that reaches them, hook_forced_normalization-Test.grug, is skipped on every server leg because the state it proves belongs to a client's frame pass.
why.net/grug/minecraft/core/GrugTestRunner$4: The seam that forwards a test's forced autosave and its forced-normalization hooks to the adapter. The autosave hook is reached only by a test whose name asks for a save tick, and that test reads the save indicator a client draws. The normalization hooks are reached only for a marked test on a client: every server leg lists hook_forced_normalization-Test.grug as unsupported, because the runner's GrugForcedNormalization.appliesTo is false on a dedicated server, which never forces the state the test's assertion is about. No test a dedicated server runs reaches them, so the entries stay.
why.net/grug/minecraft/core/ModLoaderAdapter: The test hooks an adapter keeps the no-op or local default for: the forced-normalization hook (canForceNormalizationForTest, forceNormalizationForTest, restoreNormalizationAfterTest, normalizationEnabledForTest) runs only for a marked test on a client. Every server leg lists that test as unsupported, because the runner's GrugForcedNormalization.appliesTo is false on a dedicated server, which never calls the hooks there. 1.20.6 keeps all four defaults on its client too, because its item draw uses its own shader path. testCamera is the client's own eye; every dedicated server's adapter overrides it to ask the joined client for that client's camera, so a server's own call to TestTickContext.camera goes through that override and never reaches the local default, which only a client runs. The dispatch's check counts a test a dedicated server ran as reaching what that test reaches on the client, so it offers these entries for removal; they stay because the marked test is skipped on every server leg and a server's camera call goes through its own override, so no server reaches these defaults. The world overlay entries (the world context, world key and HUD host functions and each adapter's overlay hooks) are reached only by overlay_world-Test.grug, which every server leg skips for the same reason.
